state: deduplicated: the pre-extraction copy has been removed from the skills plugin, so one qualified name resolves
verdict: EXTRACTION PASSES AT PARITY. Matches the documented pre-extraction baseline of 22/22 on the same harness, same model, same seed, same split.
why_raw_was_wrong: The runner compared the router's chosen skill name to --target by exact string. After extraction the router answers as 'asking-users-questions', not 'skills:asking-users-questions', so every hit scored as a miss.
wonBy proved it: all 10 should-trigger queries were won by this skill, 3 runs of 3 on 8 of them.

Fixed in the runner: comparison is now on the last path segment, so one skill answering under more than one qualified name cannot silently score zero. Both stored runs rescore correctly under the patch.
a_second_finding_worth_keeping: Before deduplication the same patched scorer gives 18/22, not 22/22. Two installed copies of one skill SPLIT its trigger rate between two names, and 4 queries landed at 0.33, below the 0.5 threshold.
So a duplicated skill actively suppresses its own measured trigger rate. That is an argument for deduplicating before measuring, independent of tidiness.
measurement_lesson: Three separate times in this build a scoring or configuration fault produced a number that read as a description defect: an invalid model id, the wrong harness, and an exact-match target string. Each time the fix was in the measurement. Probe the harness before editing prose.
